title: The Frog Model on $\mathbb Z$ with Random Discrete Weibull Lifetimes and Biased Nearest-Neighbour Random Walks
summary: We study the frog model on $\mathbb Z$ with particle-wise random discrete Weibull lifetimes and biased nearest-neighbour random walks. Each particle has an independent survival parameter $π\in(0,1)$. Conditionally on $π=p$, its lifetime $Ξ$ satisfies $$ \mathbb P(Ξ\ge k\mid π=p)=p^{k^γ}, \, k\in\mathbb{N}_0, $$ where $γ>0$. The distribution of $π$ is assumed to have right-edge density $$ f_π(u)\sim (1-u)^{β-1} L\left(\frac1{1-u}\right), \, u\uparrow1, $$ where $β>0$ and $L:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ is a slowly varying function at infinity.
